title: Canada Issues 7,511 Express Entry Invitations in Three-Day Draw Cluster
excerpt: IRCC held back-to-back PNP, Canadian Experience Class, and French-language draws from July 20-22, pushing total 2026 invitations past 104,000 as the Express Entry pool shrank to 231,533 candidates.
body:
Canada's immigration department conducted three Express Entry draws in three days last week, issuing a combined 7,511 invitations to apply for permanent residence between July 20 and July 22. The sequence — a Provincial Nominee Program round, a Canadian Experience Class round, and a French-language proficiency round — follows the draw-cluster pattern IRCC has favored throughout 2026.

What Happened in the July 20-22 Draws

The burst began on July 20 with a PNP draw that invited 511 candidates at a CRS cutoff of 744. The following day, IRCC targeted Canadian Experience Class candidates, issuing 2,000 invitations at a minimum CRS of 516. The cluster closed on July 22 with a French-language proficiency draw that sent out 5,000 invitations at a CRS floor of 399 — a 21-point drop from the previous French round on July 9.

The July 21 CEC draw was the 12th of its kind in 2026 and the 428th Express Entry round overall. Its 516 cutoff marked a single-point decline from the July 7 round, which invited the same number of candidates at 517. A tie-breaking rule set at May 26, 2026 at 5:33 p.m. UTC determined which profiles at the cutoff score received invitations.

"The CEC cutoff has now held within a narrow band around 515-518 for several months, even as the overall Express Entry pool has continued to grow."

— Immigration.ca analysis

Express Entry Pool Composition

As of July 19, the Express Entry pool held 231,533 active profiles, down from 235,127 on July 5 — a decrease of 3,594. The shrinkage was driven by four draws conducted between those dates that cumulatively issued more than 8,000 invitations, including the large July 7 CEC and July 9 French rounds.

The 451-500 CRS band remains the most densely populated segment of the pool, with 72,579 candidates — nearly one-third of all profiles. Another 63,877 candidates sit in the 401-450 range. Together, these two bands account for roughly 59% of the entire pool, creating a wall of competition that explains why CEC cutoffs have stabilized above 507.

The 501-600 band holds 18,133 profiles, while only 511 candidates score above 600, nearly all of whom hold provincial nominations that add an automatic 600-point boost.

2026 Invitation Pace

With the July 22 French draw, IRCC has now issued approximately 104,612 invitations across 41 Express Entry rounds in 2026. CEC draws alone account for roughly 45,250 of those, making the Canadian Experience Class the single largest source of invitations this year.

French-language draws have issued about 40,500 invitations across eight rounds in 2026, with cutoffs ranging from 393 to 420. PNP rounds, while frequent, issue far fewer invitations per draw — typically 300 to 950 — but at much higher CRS cutoffs that reflect the 600-point nomination bonus.

What This Means for Indian Applicants

Indians consistently form the largest nationality group in the Express Entry pool. For CEC-eligible candidates with scores between 507 and 515, the stable cutoff band is both frustrating and encouraging — frustrating because the margin is razor-thin, but encouraging because a single improvement in language scores or an additional year of Canadian work experience could push a profile over the line.

Candidates scoring below 500 face longer odds in CEC rounds at current volumes. Provincial nominations remain the most powerful lever, effectively guaranteeing an invitation once secured. Healthcare and trades category draws, which have operated with cutoffs in the 467-477 range this year, offer alternative pathways for candidates in qualifying occupations.

What Comes Next

IRCC's 2026 draw calendar suggests category-based rounds will continue to follow CEC and PNP clusters. A healthcare or trades draw could come within days if IRCC maintains its recent cadence. The department has also introduced new categories this year — physicians with Canadian work experience, senior managers, and researchers — that have operated at lower CRS thresholds.

Candidates who received invitations in the July 20-22 draws have 60 days to submit complete permanent residence applications, which are typically processed within a six-month service standard. Those still in the pool should ensure their profiles remain current and language test results valid, as IRCC has shown no signs of slowing its pace of draws heading into the second half of 2026.
